svg.text: Miniforge Target — T2. Run Hierarchy, Loops, Governance
Spec → MiniforgeRun → WorkflowRun DAG → TaskNode/AgentSession · three nested loops · packs → gates → evidence · the intervention round-trip
RUN HIERARCHY (N5-delta-3)
Spec — the supervisory root
human intent + constraints; prose → LLM → EDN
"How is N13 going?" is a question about a Spec
:spec/* = intent (user-authored)
MiniforgeRun — one execution of a spec
budgeted, resumable, evidence-bearing
WorkflowRun — ~40 in a DAG per run
each a full process instance with its own FSM;
:workflow/* = process · :task/* = decomposed work
TaskNode + AgentSession (orchestrated leaf)
the unit an agent actually executes; OCI capsule;
sub-pipeline explore→plan→implement→verify
Bare agents join the hierarchy
non-miniforge sessions (Claude Code, codex) are first-class
supervised entities, observed by Rust adapters tailing
vendor telemetry:
Discovered → Watching → Blocked → Idle →
Completed / Failed → Unreachable
the console supervises work it didn't launch
THREE NESTED LOOPS (product-vision · N5-delta-2)
Loop 0 — inner (the agent's own loop)
plan → implement → test → review → release
validate-and-repair until gates pass; budget-bounded; no human
as-built today — panel A2 is this loop
Loop 1 — outer (PR monitor)
watches the open PR: resolves feedback, pushes fixes, manages
budget, escalates when stuck (pr-lifecycle + pr-train as-built;
the fully autonomous monitor is the designed version)
Loop 2 — META AGENTS (doormen over meaning)
a set of meta agents gate SEMANTIC INTENT and run specialized
reviews: did the agent build something DIFFERENT than planned?
("IMPORT spec ⇒ 0 creates" lives here) — a perfectly built
wrong thing fails · meta-evaluator + coordinator (as-built roster)
Loop 3 — META-META: the operator (plumbed, nearing release)
the operator component orchestrates the meta loop itself;
the human supervises it from the console — pause · resume · cancel ·
retry · waive — always through the intervention round-trip (right)
FSM roster — 10 machines on one fsm component
execution · supervision · degradation · pr-lifecycle · task ·
dag-task · inner-loop · agent-lifecycle · heuristic · circuit-breaker
ONE phase authority: the workflow FSM (current-phase-id) — all others observe, feeding back only via the orchestrator
GOVERNANCE & DURABILITY
policy packs → gates → evidence bundles
per-rule :rule/enforcement — hard-halt · require-approval · warn · audit
COMPILED packs (policy-pack/compiler) drive gates wired fail-closed at every
transition (as-built); evidence bundles carry provenance + semantic intent
fail-open RESOLVED (Ariadne step 1, #1555–#1558): unknown vocabulary now denies — T3 #4
trust model
:authority/data vs :authority/instruction · levels: tainted · untrusted · trusted
instructions and data are typed differently at the boundary — the same
injection discipline the tenancy architecture formalizes
The intervention round-trip (normative)
every supervisory write MUST materialize as an InterventionRequest
before application
no side-channel commands: the operator's pause/waive/cancel is itself a
first-class, auditable entity with a lifecycle — commands leave receipts
structurally preserved for the Fleet multi-operator case (deferred)
Durability — "the event stream IS the product surface"
append-only event stream · evidence bundles · worktree-diff-as-artifact ·
operator append-only journal
everything the console shows is a projection over the stream; replay is
first-class (Rust state store: replay + snowflake ids)
run-model repo (miniforge-run-specs) is EMPTY — the run model lives in the N-specs (see T3)
How the planes meet the loops
Loop 0 lives in Plane 1 (the engine). Loop 1 spans engine ↔ forge. Loops 2/3 live in Plane 2 (the console), commanding through the intervention
round-trip. Fleet (Plane 3) coordinates many engines but never blocks them. The eval seam (Plane 5) judges outcomes across products — the same
workbench snapshot that grades career grades miniforge governance itself.
TYPES
run-hierarchy entity
loop
state machine roster
governance
normative contract / durability
